channel.title: 个人数学雷达
channel.description: 数学、形式化证明与 AI for Math；来源原文摘录及中文译文

item.title: The Power of Beauty and Elegance
item.description: What machines have: colossal knowledge and massive compute power. What humans have: intuition for beauty and elegance. The ultimate question is whether colossal knowledge and massive compute power wins over human intuition. If no, we only face some big changes. If yes, then human mathematics will degrade into exotic art.

item.title: 代理强化学习中的数据如何扩展：法则和综合策略
item.description: 预训练缩放法则将训练数据视为一维数量：令牌计数。代理强化学习（RL）继承了这种标量抽象，但现代综合管道现在以非常不同的成本独立生成 \textit{tasks}、\textit{environments} 和 \textit{trajectories}，将数据转换为结构化设计空间。这就提出了一个预训练从来不需要回答的问题：给定综合预算，\textit{哪个轴}应该缩放？我们通过三个紧密耦合的贡献来端到端地解决这个问题。首先，我们将代理数据分解为三个基数轴（任务、环境、轨迹），加上奖励密度控制变量，并在跨数学+代码、SWE、Web 和 UI/工具应用程序域的不同大型语言模型 (LLM) 上拟合每轴缩放关系。在我们测量的所有模型大小、模型系列、领域和 RL 算法（PPO 和 GRPO）中，缩放指数顺序为环境 $>$ 任务 $>$ 轨迹。当环境多样性分解为世界多样性和环境结构多样性时，其优势主要由前者驱动，而后者只是由环境多样性驱动。

item.title: 通过进化策略进行持续的测试时学习
item.description: 大型语言模型越来越多地在开放环境中运行，在这种环境中，它们需要不断适应不断变化的任务和分布，而通常不需要外部监督。现有的持续学习方法依赖于外部监督，例如标记数据、演示或奖励信号，这在实践中可能成本高昂或不可用。测试时适应通过从自我生成的监督中学习来消除这种依赖性，但现有的方法从正在更新的单个策略中获得监督，因此一旦策略发生变化，其自身的学习信号也会随之变化，从而导致策略崩溃、推理退化和灾难性遗忘。在本文中，我们提出了 \textbf{进化策略强化学习（ESRL）}，这是一种持续的测试时间学习框架，它从一组策略而不是单个正在训练的策略中获取自我生成的监督。 ESRL 扰乱参数空间中的锚定策略，以形成附近策略的群体，从每个策略中采样一个轨迹，并将其答案聚合成中央策略的无标签组相关学习信号。

item.title: 混合依赖下投票分类器的保证金证书

item.title: 通过高斯加权脊波变换的无限维神经网络的构造通用逼近
item.description: 输入为函数的神经网络（如算子学习）通常通过存在性论证（通过简化为有限维网络或通过 Stone-Weierstrass 型密度）证明是普遍的；这些证明了近似值的存在，但很少说明参数如何依赖于目标。我们采取建设性路线。我们将脊波变换（一种与傅立叶变换、氡变换和小波变换相关的积分变换）扩展到可分离的无限维希尔伯特空间上的连续映射，用方向空间上的均匀混合的高斯权重替换在无限维中不可用的勒贝格测度。生成的变换具有 Plancherel 恒等式和重建公式，其中包含帧算子、权重引起的校正，并且它为每个目标分配一个显式系数测量，每个可允许的分析滤波器都有一个。从这些表示中，我们获得了多项式增长的所有连续非多项式激活的紧集的一致近似，包括 ReLU，并且通过系数的蒙特卡罗采样，有限宽度网络

item.title: 以最佳速率和规模均匀收敛
item.description: 均匀收敛询问有多少随机样本足以使经验平均值同时逼近整个函数类的期望。它是概率的核心概念，也是统计学习的基础。对于二值类，Vapnik--Chervonenkis 定理通过 VC 维度的有限性来表征一致收敛。对于维度 $d$，加性误差 $\varepsilon$ 的最坏情况样本复杂度为 $d/\varepsilon^2$。对于实值函数，类似的组合参数是脂肪粉碎维度，它取决于近似尺度 $\gamma$。挑战是用 $d/\varepsilon^2$ 样本实现错误 $\gamma+\varepsilon$，匹配二进制类的样本范围，其中 $d$ 现在是规模 $\gamma$ 上的脂肪粉碎维度。以前的结果要么实现了最佳规模，要么实现了最佳样本复杂性，但不能同时实现两者。我们的主要结果弥补了这一差距，在最佳规模下建立了尖锐的样本复杂性。在此过程中，我们使用了几种可能具有独立兴趣的工具。第一个涉及 $\varepsilon$-nets

item.title: 衡量离线数据对内在驱动探索的授权
item.description: 先前经验的大型未标记数据集越来越多地可用于机器人和编码等领域的代理任务。这些任务的常见方法是使用先前的数据训练策略，然后通过在线部署进一步改进它。但是，虽然很多工作都在研究如何使用离线和在线数据进行策略提取，但在理解在线学习阶段如何使用先验数据有效地\textit{explore}方面所做的工作却少之又少。之前的工作试图通过定义 \textit{empowerment} 来形式化这个想法，这是一个衡量智能体可以实现多少种未来状态的指标；权力较高的国家需要更多的探索，因为有更多的未来可供探索。然而，现有的评估赋权的方法需要在环境中在线推出政策。我们提出了第一种方法，用于根据未标记的先验数据来估计赋权，而无需任何环境交互。通过共同学习赋权最大化策略及其折扣状态占用度量，我们的估计器可以接受由任何未知数生成的未标记轨迹的训练。

item.title: 库存限制下连续做市的无悔收入最大化
item.description: 做市商通过为买家和卖家设定出价和要价来保持交易效率。在顺序做市中，交易根据价格阈值独立发生，要求做市商在 T 轮中保持平衡、低风险的库存。本文研究了如何使用后悔最小化在未知的买家和卖家估值的情况下最大化收入。当做市商只看到交易成功或失败时，算法会实现遗憾，库存范围与 T 的 2/3 次方成正比。当失败交易的完整订单簿数据可用时，遗憾和库存限制将显着改善至 T 的平方根。我们还通过下限建立基本权衡，证明更严格的逐轮库存限制严格迫使更高的最小遗憾。

item.title: 使用上下文管理和外部存储器进行推理
item.description: 推理模型通过上下文记忆维护有关其推理过程状态的信息。复杂的问题需要更大的上下文窗口和内存需求。在这种情况下，没有缓存的上下文管理可能会丢弃用于推理的有用信息。我们提出了 RCMEM，这是一种使用外部存储器扩展上下文管理的方法，以维护附加信息，而不会给推理模型带来附加上下文的负担。 RCMEM 显着减少了需要重复计算中间步骤的问题的计算时间，同时在复杂问题上实现了更好的性能。我们使用 0.4 到 2500 万参数的模型大小和 GPT-2 演示了我们解决一些数学问题的方法。

item.title: 通过自适应重放保持强化学习中的推理多样性并提供可验证的奖励
item.description: 带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）提高了大型语言模型的推理能力，但往往降低了其推理行为的多样性。我们从有限样本学习动态的角度研究这种现象，并表明有限的策略推出可以逐渐抑制语义上不同但同样奖励的推理模式。一旦某个模式变得足够欠采样，标准同策略 RLVR 很少能恢复它。受这一观察的启发，我们提出了 TAR，一种有针对性的自适应重放框架，它保留了基本策略中已经存在的各种正确推理行为。 TAR 构建了一个包含不同基本模型解决方案的紧凑存储库，并通过自适应机制选择性地重放它们，该机制仅在 RLVR 期间抑制存储的行为时激活。在六个数学推理基准和两个 Qwen2.5 模型尺度上，TAR 始终比现有的多样性保留后训练方法在推理性能和多样性保留之间取得了更好的平衡，同时大大减少了正确基础模型的遗忘

item.title: 从故事到特征：缩放概念向量以实现人工智能对齐和可解释性
item.description: 我们研究特征向量：语言模型激活空间中与人类可解释的概念相对应的方向，例如诚实或欺骗。现有的无监督方法（例如稀疏自动编码器）试图恢复整个特征空间，通常以特征质量和可解释性为代价。我们采取了更务实的路线：专注于与人工智能安全和对齐相关的概念，我们生成合成的概念-对抗故事对，并使用它们的平均模型激活的差异作为特征向量。我们使用公开发布的跨多种语言和流派的 2M 合成故事，将此方法扩展到 1,036 个与对齐相关的概念。在三个模型系列的六个模型中，我们的特征向量可靠地概括为检测聊天对话和网络文本中相应的概念。它们形成跨模型共享的可解释几何形状，并且在注入激活时可以因果地引导模型行为。我们进一步使用这些功能来分析越狱攻击、数学和代理推理期间的模型表示。因此，我们的目标特征构建提供了可扩展的

item.title: 使用密码进行培训以增强稀有语言翻译的上下文术语学习
item.description: 使用上下文示例（IC-Train）微调法学硕士可以让翻译模型在部署时适应新的并行数据，但尚不清楚它们是否真的从这些示例中学习了罕见术语的翻译。我们将这种能力正式化为上下文术语学习（ICTL）。我们表明标准 IC-Train 只能弱地开发这种能力，并提出 RareCipherFT，它在没有任何词汇资源的情况下增强了这种能力。 RareCipherFT 将每个训练目标与与其共享稀有术语的上下文示例配对。然后，它在上下文和引用中都用字符打乱的密码替换该术语，因此只能通过从上下文复制来恢复该术语。训练数据的加密部分被退火以保持翻译质量。在英语和泰米尔语、阿萨姆语、米佐语、尼泊尔语和豪萨语之间的七个翻译方向以及从 1B 到 7B 参数的四个模型中，RareCipherFT 比标准 IC-Train 提高了术语召回率 5-15 个绝对点，而没有降低 COMET。使用同义词、随机数词和共享表面上下文控制的探测表明，这些收益来自于将源术语与其内部术语联系起来。

item.title: 强化学习给推理带来了什么：一些基本模型不会做出的决定
item.description: 具有可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）极大地改善了数学推理，但它对基本模型的添加内容仍不清楚。我们通过对 Qwen3-4B-Base 进行一系列生成时间干预来研究这一问题，测量每次干预在 120 个 AIME 问题上恢复了多少经过 RL 训练的对应增益。具有相同 8,192 个令牌输出限制的功率采样不会带来除贪婪解码之外的任何增益。然而，仅在两个模型的贪婪选择不同的情况下借用 RL 模型的代币（生成头寸的大约 4%），即可恢复 pass@1 收益的 90.5%，在 MATH-500 上的三个模型对上也有类似的恢复。我们发现，即使是单个开头标记也会产生重大影响：强制基本模型以“好吧”开始可以恢复 35% 的 RL 增益。然而，仅开口是不够的。在相同的空缺之后的后续替换又为 pass@1 添加了 5.2 个百分点，而我们测试的插入反射词（例如“等待”）的固定规则并没有重现这一好处。稀疏替换还保留了基本模型的大部分多样性，同时在 pass@1 上保持接近 RL 模型。在

item.title: BanglaBBQ：孟加拉国背景下问答的偏见基准
item.description: 本文介绍了 BanglaBBQ，这是一个问答偏见基准，旨在捕捉孟加拉语和英语中基于孟加拉语的刻板印象。继 KoBBQ 和 PakBBQ 之后，BanglaBBQ 通过将其模板分为三组来适应原始的问答偏差基准 (BBQ)：直接翻译 (DT)、修改为使目标群体或上下文与孟加拉国语 (TM) 保持一致，以及在认为不适合孟加拉国语境时删除 (SR)。此过程保留了 6 个类别的 140 个模板，其中包括 76 个 DT 模板和 64 个 TM 模板。然后根据孟加拉国社会常见的刻板印象，添加了五个新创建的（NA）类别：婚姻状况、年龄和政治观念、地区出身、教育背景和心理健康状况。孟加拉国本土注释者对所有 466 个新编写的模板进行了评判，其中 372 个被保留，因为绝大多数英语注释者确定了预期目标并将这种态度评为足够普遍。每个新创作的模板都链接到记录的来源和逐字引用。每个评估模板还具有反刻板印象

item.title: 法学硕士能够用语言表达数学公式吗？多领域评估
item.description: 大型语言模型 (LLM) 在自然语言任务中表现出了强大的能力。但他们生成准确的数学公式书面表达的能力尚未得到系统评估。这种语言表达对于支持基于音频的学习和视障用户的文本到语音系统非常重要。我们评估了六个科学领域的五位最先进的法学硕士，并构建了 Read-Aloud Math，这是一个平衡的多领域语料库，包含 LaTeX 公式、手动验证的简单和扩展转录、多个变体、文本上下文、领域标签和公式复杂性级别。使用多参考 BLEU，GPT-5.2 在简单转录方面取得了最高分（无上下文时为 75.9%，有上下文时为 64.9%），尽管在无上下文时它的表现并没有显着优于 Grok 4.1 Fast 或 Claude Sonnet 4.5。 Claude Sonnet 4.5 在没有上下文的扩展转录方面获得了最高分 (36.5%)，而 Grok 4.1 Fast 在有上下文的情况下获得了最高分 (48.8%)。对于扩展转录，统计和数学在两种背景设置中得分最高，而物理得分最低。公式长度为 si

item.title: Epi：走向持久的、自我改进的自主研究代理
item.description: 我们提出 \'{E}pi，一个自主研究代理，它可以维持跨模型会话的调查，并通过积累的经验改进其方法。 \'{E}pi 结合了持久的研究历史、分层记忆、分支和独立审查，以保持研究的连续性、从实验中学习、探索和重新审视替代方法。它的实验跨越会话边界，并且固定的验证器评估它们的输出。 \'{E}pi 产生了 120 项创纪录的结果，其中包括 12 个家庭的 20 项数字绑定记录和 8 个家庭的 100 项建筑记录。其中包括 $n$-queens 常数的约 84 倍窄区间和四次费根鲍姆吸引子维数的 360 万倍窄严格区间。精确的双重证明表明，Cohn-Elkies 线性规划界限在 10 维和 11 维上不可能是锐利的。除了数值改进之外，\'{E}pi 还给出了 Tuza 猜想的计算机辅助证明，用于具有八个顶点团部分和最多三个三角形活跃邻域类型的分裂图，具有任意重数。我们

item.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
item.description: For a fixed integer $a>0$, consider the shifted truncations \[ F_{n,a}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!} \] and their monic integral normalizations $P_{n,a}(x)=(n+a)!F_{n,a}(x)$. In this paper, we prove that, for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible has natural density one. We also prove that $G_{n,a}:=\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})$ is primitive for all sufficiently large $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible, and that it contains $A_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. Finally, we prove that, for any fixed integer $a>0$, the discriminant of $F_{n,a}$ is a nonsquare for a density-one set of $n$, and hence that $\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})=S_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. To obtain irreducibility with density one, we use a result of Shorey and Tijdeman, as well as a smooth-number density argument. Following that, two explicitly chosen Newton polygons give cycles that force primitivity, and hence containment of $A_n$. item.title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
item.description: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Trevi\~no's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

item.title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
item.description: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos(2\pi y)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.

item.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
item.description: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued

item.title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
item.description: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.

item.title: Quantum Variance for Hecke--Maass Cusp Forms on the Vertical Geodesic
item.description: Let $X=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H$, and let $\{u_j\}$ be an orthonormal basis of even Hecke--Maass cusp forms on $X$ with Laplace eigenvalues $1/4+t_j^2$. For a real-valued $\psi\in C_c^\infty(0,\infty)$, define \[ \mu_j(\psi)=\int_0^\infty\psi(y)|u_j(iy)|^2\,\frac{dy}{y}, \qquad M(\psi)=\frac6\pi\int_0^\infty\psi(y)\,\frac{dy}{y}. \] For $T\ge2$, $1\le U\le T$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove \[ \sum_{\substack{u_j\ {\rm even}\\T<\theta\le1$, $0<\eta<\theta/2$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, if $T^\theta\le U\le T$, then all but \[ O_{\psi,\theta,\eta,\varepsilon} \!\left(T^{1+2\eta+\varepsilon}\right) \] of the even forms with $T<t_j\le T+U$ satisfy $\mu_j(\psi)=M(\psi)+O(T^{-\eta})$. In particular, the exceptional proportion tends to zero in this short spectral interval.

item.title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
item.description: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.

item.title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
item.description: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.

item.title: Metric dimension and maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of graph Laplacians
item.description: We study equality between metric dimension and the maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. These quantities are not ordered in general. Using the standard decomposition associated with twin classes, we separate forced multiplicities from quotient-spectrum contributions. We give complete equality classifications for complete multipartite graphs and core--satellite graphs, and enumerate the multipartite equality graphs by order. For graphs formed by attaching at least two leaves to every vertex of a connected core, the metric dimension and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $ 1 $ are known; we show that this multiplicity is maximal for both matrices, and uniquely maximal except for $ P_3 $. We enumerate this core--leaf family up to isomorphism and obtain a uniform asymptotic formula by order and metric dimension, together with the quadratic exponential growth rate $ 1/18 $. An exact census of connected graphs of orders two through seven identifies the first separating examples and examples without twins. Finally, for every odd $ r \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3} $, we study $ \Theta_{2, 2, r} $ and dete

item.title: A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton
item.description: We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that $\frac{1-q}{(q^n;q)_m}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}$ has nonnegative power-series coefficients for $0 <n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. We obtain a polynomial version by bounding a M\"obius correction by first differences of Gaussian coefficients. The proof uses partitions and quadratic and cubic semi-invariants of binary forms. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner--Stanton--White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

item.title: Vertex Removal and Vertex-Edge Domination
item.description: A vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ $ve$-dominates every edge incident with a vertex in its closed neighborhood $N_{G}[v]$. A set of vertices is a vertex-edge dominating set ($ve$-dominating set) if every edge of $G$ is $ve$-dominated by some vertex in the set. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the vertex-edge domination number $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, also known as the isolation number. In this paper, we study the effect of vertex removal on $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, establish sharp bounds on $\gamma_{ve}(G-v)$ and characterize the vertices whose removal decreases, preserves, or increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$. Let $V^0(G)$ and $V^+(G)$ denote the sets of vertices whose removal preserves and increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, respectively, and let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ consist of the vertices in $V^0(G)$ belonging to every minimum $ve$-dominating set. We prove that \[ |V^0(G)|\geq3|V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)|+\sum_{v\in V^+(G)} \bigl(\gamma_{ve}(G-v)-\gamma_{ve}(G)+1\bigr). \] In particular, $|V^0(G)|\geq 2|V^+(G)|$. We also prove that every vertex in $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ lies on a cycle and that $V^0(T)\neq\emptyset$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three.

item.title: Gaussian Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums in Higher Dimensions
item.description: For sequences of $n$ nonnegative integer vectors in $\mathbb Z^k$ with distinct subset sums, we prove, for fixed $k$, the uniform lower bound $M\ge (C_k-o(1))2^{n/k}/\sqrt n$ for the largest coordinate, where \[ C_k=\sqrt{\frac{2k}{\pi}}\, \frac{(k+1)^{(k-1)/(2k)}}{\sqrt{\lfloor (k+1)^2/4\rfloor}}. \] The proof compares a Gaussian-kernel expectation with a sum over a translated lattice, uniformly over the vector sequence. We optimise the resulting quadratic-form constant using a vertex second-moment certificate. We show that $C_k$ also exceeds the variance constant obtained by optimising an ellipsoidal geometry.

item.title: Partitionability is NP-complete
item.description: We show that the problem of deciding whether a simplicial complex is partitionable is NP-complete in dimensions two and higher, answering a 1995 question of Kleinschmidt and Onn.

item.title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
item.description: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.

item.title: Subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs
item.description: Since their introduction by Karo\'nski, Scheinerman, and Singer-Cohen in 90's, random intersection graphs have attracted much attention, mostly due to their various applications. In this article, we establish a general result for the probability that a given small subgraph is present in a random intersection graph. Our theorem applies to a broad range of parameters, including regimes that have not previously been considered in the literature. Moreover, it extends known results and situates them within a broader framework, making this approach a convenient tool for comparing the probabilities of graphs in the random intersection graph model. To prove our main result, we develop new proof techniques that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been employed in the study of small subgraphs in random intersection graphs. Many special cases and examples are presented as well.

item.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of cliques
item.description: Let $X^{(r)}_n$ denote the number of copies of a complete graph $K_r$ in the random intersection graph model on $n$ vertices. We derive upper bounds on the distance between the standardized version of $X^{(r)}_n$ and the standard normal distribution, measured in both the Kolmogorov and Wasserstein metrics. We complement these results with necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality. As a byproduct, we provide precise estimates for the variance of $X^{(r)}_n$. In the process, we develop new general techniques for analysing so--called clique covers, which play a crucial role in the study of subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs.

item.title: The integral $K_0$-ring of the stack of smooth hyperelliptic curves
item.description: We compute the integral $K_0$-ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr H_g$ of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g\ge2$ over a field of characteristic zero. We show that it is a free abelian group of rank $8g+2$ for even $g$ and $8g+4$ for odd $g$. We use the isotypic decomposition of the $K_0$ of a related $\mu_{g+1}$-gerbe to obtain presentations for both even and odd $g$'s from the standard quotient presentation of $\mathscr H_g$. Thus, our technique differs from the $CH^\bullet(\mathscr H_g)$ computations of Edidin--Fulghesu, Fulghesu--Viviani, Di Lorenzo, and the $K_0(\mathscr M_2)$ computation of Edidin--Hu. Using Pagani's description of the inertia stack of $\mathscr H_g$, we apply Riemann--Roch to interpret the rank of $K_0(\mathscr H_g)$ as the number of inertia components. Finally, we compare the $K_0$ and Chow rings of $\mathscr H_g$ through the gamma-filtration and give presentations to the associated graded rings $\operatorname{gr}_{\gamma}K_0(\mathscr H_g)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$.

item.title: Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models
item.description: We establish a strong Hodge decomposition theorem for Novikov type Landau--Ginzburg models, that is, triples $(M,g,\theta)$ consisting of a non-compact complete K\"ahler manifold $(M,g)$ and a non-trivial closed holomorphic one-form $\theta$ on $M$.Under the well-tameness condition and under the assumption that $M$ is Stein, we prove that the space of $L^{2}$-forms on $M$ admits an orthogonal decomposition into the space of harmonic forms of the twisted Laplacian $\Delta_{\theta}$ and the images of the twisted Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial+\theta\wedge$ and $\bar\partial^{\dagger}+\iota_{\bar\theta^{\sharp}}$; moreover, the harmonic space is concentrated in degree $n=\dim_{\C}M$ and is isomorphic to the Milnor rings of $\theta$. As applications, we endow the complement of a hyperplane arrangement with a complete cylindrical K\"ahler metric, and we show that the differential of a master function with nonresonant weights is well-tamed with respect to this metric. After passing to a log resolution in the non-normal-crossing case; we then apply the results to the Yang--Yang functional of the Gaudin model, whose critical points are the

item.title: Secondary Chow Invariants beyond Lawson--Massey Products
item.description: We construct secondary Chow invariants that cannot be recovered from Lawson--Massey realization. For every smooth complex projective curve $C$ of positive genus and every $n\ge2$, explicit cubical defining systems yield $n$ distinct Massey values in $\rm{CH}^{3}(C\times P^{2},1)$, with zero full indeterminacy, forming a cyclic group of order $n$. All corresponding triples have identical morphic classes and zero morphic, Lawson, and singular Massey brackets, despite nonzero target groups. The values are detected by the Weil pairing. We further construct secondary quotient classes of every finite order on smooth projective varieties with ample canonical bundle in every dimension at least two, and prove that generically finite pullbacks of coprime degree preserve their exact orders. These constructions obstruct integral and prime-local motivic formality, although the corresponding brackets become $\{0\}$ after reduction modulo every integer $m\ge2$. All specified values are torsion and vanish after rationalization.

item.title: Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veroneseans
item.description: The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. We also show that many Terracini loci involve only sets with "intratangent pairs" that lie on the same tangent space to the underlying Veronese variety. Finally, we give some applications to algebraic statistics, showing that osculating varieties of Veronese varieties are moment varieties for local mixtures of location families and connecting Terracini loci to local identifiability.

item.title: Nef complexity of klt Fano varieties: the full spectrum and classification below two
item.description: Let $X$ be a complex klt Fano variety. We study the rational total index $\tau_X$ and the nef complexity $c_X=\dim X+\rho(X)-\tau_X$. Previous joint work of the author with Enwright, Filipazzi, Gongyo, Moraga, Svaldi, and Wang established the corresponding nonnegativity and zero-case characterization in the broader framework of a special class of generalized log Calabi--Yau pairs. Here we give a direct proof in the Fano setting, prove that there is no value strictly between zero and one, and classify all klt Fano varieties with $c_X<2$, without assuming $\mathbb Q$-factoriality. At complexity one, after splitting off projective-space factors, the remaining factor is a normal quadric of Picard number one, a linear blow-up of projective space, or an integral $(1,1)$ hypersurface in a product of projective spaces. If $1<2$, only two weighted-projective families occur; in particular, no smooth Fano variety has nef complexity strictly between one and two. We also determine the spectrum when the dimension is allowed to vary: \[ \{0\}\cup\left\{2-\frac2q \ \middle| \ q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq2}\right\} \cup(\mathbb Q\cap[2,\infty)). \] Most proofs

item.title: Lattice Moduli and Residual Atoms
item.description: We study prescribed holomorphic lattices for regular-singular connections and residual factors of quantum $F$-bundles. For an arbitrary ordered monodromy spectrum, we classify the fully framed local groupoid: each residue fibre is a discrete affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$, with a unique normal form and trivial stabilisers. We then analyse elementary changes of lattice. A strictly positive integral residue difference obstructs the oriented wall; otherwise, in arbitrary rank, the extending normal-form arcs form an affine torsor of relative dimension $r(r-1)$, and specialisation to the shifted residue slice is polynomial and triangular by root height. Adjacent walls exhibit the composite-root correction dictated by the type-$A$ root-subgroup relations, while an example over the dual numbers detects a nilpotent saturation defect. For one-branch $F$-bundles, the scalar branch is recovered from the residual trace, and scalar residualisation yields a symmetric monoidal equivalence with zero-branch $F$-bundles. This construction yields residual atoms, functorial Jordan strata, and a residual chemical formula compatible with blow-ups and p

item.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
item.description: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

item.title: Rational analytic prismatization
item.description: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory

item.title: Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes
item.description: In this paper, we focuses on how the distribution of random step sizes affects Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes. First, with sub-exponential moment condition of random step sizes, we establish Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviation results. Consequently, moderate deviation principles are obtained. Secondly, for random step sizes with sub-exponential tails, we establish a large deviation principle on tail probabilities. Finally, for random step sizes with regularly varying tails, we obtain precise large deviations.

item.title: Least singular values of Gaussian matrices with deterministic shifts
item.description: Let $A$ be a deterministic real square matrix and $G$ a standard Gaussian matrix. We determine $\E\smin(A+G)$, up to universal constants, in terms of the singular values of $A$. The expectation is comparable to the square root of the smallest zero of the expected characteristic polynomial of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$. This resolves Problem~3 in Tikhomirov's ICM 2022 survey. We also prove that the zeros of the expected characteristic polynomial are majorized by the expected ordered eigenvalues of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$.

item.title: Supercritical Branching Random Walks on Nested Lattices
item.description: In classical models of supercritical continuous-time branching random walks (BRWs) on a $d$-dimensional lattice, the dimension $d$ is typically assumed to be fixed. When comparing the exponential growth rate $\lambda_0$ of a particle population in a BRW with a single branching source across lattices of different dimensions, a question arises whether it is possible to construct a family of random walks on $d$-dimensional lattices such that the model for a $(d+1)$-dimensional lattice ``inherits'' the properties of the model for a $d$-dimensional lattice in a meaningful sense. To address this question, the paper introduces the concept of a ``random walk on nested lattices'' and investigates the effect of the dimension $d$ on particle population growth using the ``inheritance'' condition. For an arbitrary symmetric random walk, a limit theorem is proved on the representation of the positive eigenvalue of the evolution operator for the mean particle numbers in terms of the process parameters and the dimension $d$, as the branching source intensity $\beta \to \infty$. The theorem shows that the influence of dimension persists even for very

item.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
item.description: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limitin

item.title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
item.description: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems.We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variant

item.title: A functional central limit theorem for the KPZ equation with narrow wedge initial data
item.description: In this article, we consider the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation with narrow wedge initial data. We prove a functional central limit theorem for the spatial average of the solution, which solves an open problem from Gu and Pu (2025). Our main tool is Clark-Ocone formula from Malliavin calculus, combined with an in-depth analysis of the increments of the solution. The main step is a moment bound for time increments of the normalized spatial integral. For this, we introduce a new technique, called a ``common-ray'' change of variables. Using the fact that Malliavin derivative of the solution satisfies a Chapman-Kolmogorov relation, we reduce the kernel differences at two times to spatial increments at one common time.

item.title: From Hermite Chaos to an Attractive Log-Gas: Explicit High-Rank Limits of Iterated-Logarithm and Tail Constants
item.description: Let $Z$ be a standard Hermite process of order $m\ge2$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$. For $d2$, let $Y$ be the variance-normalized version of the weighted integral $\int_0^1 x^{-d}\,\mathrm dZ(x)$. Its right tail satisfies $ \log\Pr\{Y>t\}\sim -\frac12\left(\frac{t}{\Lambda_m}\right)^{2m}, t\to\infty, $ where the positive constant $\Lambda_m$ admits an infinite-dimensional variational representation. The same constant governs the sharp law of the iterated logarithm for weighted sums of nonlinear functions of long-memory Gaussian sequences. A general closed-form evaluation at finite order is not known. As $m\to\infty$ with $H$ and $d$ fixed, the normalized constants $\sqrt{m!}\,\Lambda_m$ decrease to an explicit positive function of $H$ and $d$, with relative error $O(m^{-1})$. This function also gives a lower bound for the normalized constant at every finite order. An exact R\'enyi variational representation at each order yields, in the high-rank limit, the entropy--energy variational problem of an attractive logarithmic gas. The limiting free energy is evaluated through the Selberg integral and the Barnes $G$ function. For $d\le0$, c

item.title: Chaotic CLT using Poisson Fourth Moment Theorem and Graph Theory
item.description: In this article, we consider the parabolic Anderson model and the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension 1, driven by a time-independent L\'evy noise, which is either white, or colored with integrable coloration kernel $\kappa$. Using a Poisson version of the Fourth Moment Theorem due to D\"obler, Vidotto and Zheng (2018), we prove that the spatial integral of the solution satisfies a central limit theorem. We prove that this result also holds for the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension $d=2$, if in addition $\kappa$ is bounded. To estimate the fourth cumulant of the projection of the spatial integral on a fixed chaos, we develop a novel technique using graph theory, which allows us to handle some intricate integrals involving the modified contractions.

item.title: Iterated Lavrentiev regularization under random noise: variational source conditions and rates in expectation
item.description: The convergence theory of iterated Lavrentiev regularization for nonlinear monotone ill-posed equations is deterministic: the data error is bounded by a known level that the discrepancy principle uses explicitly. Under Gaussian noise no such bound exists. For a discretized two-dimensional nonlinear inverse source problem for the Poisson equation, we analyse convergence in a finite-energy Gaussian noise model, keeping the linearized and nonlinear cases apart. For the linearized iteration the noisy and noise-free iterates differ by one resolvent applied to the noise; this gives an exact singular-value variance formula, a priori rates in expectation, and the main result: for a family of discretizations whose distance functions are bounded uniformly in the mesh, the rate is governed by that decay, which relaxes the classical range condition. The rate degrades gracefully, down to logarithmic, as the underlying continuum error loses smoothness, and a balancing rule attains it without knowing the smoothness. For the full nonlinear iteration under the order-one source condition, a truncated discrepancy principle fed only the noise level attai

item.title: A noise-level-free parameter-choice rule for iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear potential monotone ill-posed problems
item.description: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations $F(x)=y$ in a Hilbert space, where $F$ is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fr\'echet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution $x^\dg$ (a locally \emph{potential} operator), and only noisy data $y^\delta$ with unknown noise norm $\delta:=\|y-y^\delta\|$ is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^\delta=x_k^\delta-\bigl(F'(x_k^\delta)+\alpha_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta+\alpha_k(x_k^\delta-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require $\delta$. We analyze a \emph{noise-level-free} parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer $k_*$ of $\theta(k,y^\delta)=\|F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta\|^2/\alpha_k^2$ over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and $\alpha_{k_*}^2\ge c\,\delta/\|x_0-x^\dg\|$. If moreover $x_0-x^\dg\in\R(F'(x^\dg))$ and $k_*\ge1$, we prove $\|x_{k_*}^\delta-x^\dg\|=O(\sqrt{\delta_*}+\sqrt{\delta})$ with the computable $\delta_*=\|F(x_{k_*}^\delta)-y^\delta\|$ satisfying $\kappa\delta\le\delta_*\le C
